Which electrons does a transition metal lose first when it forms an ion?
back: The 4s electrons, then 3d. E.g. Fe [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s² → Fe²⁺ [Ar] 3d⁶ → Fe³⁺ [Ar] 3d⁵.

front: Why do electrons occupy equal-energy orbitals singly before pairing?
back: Two electrons in one orbital repel (spin-pair repulsion); being in separate orbitals with parallel spins gives lower energy.

front: Shapes of s and p orbitals?
back: s: spherical. p: dumbbell-shaped, three per sub-shell at right angles (px, py, pz).
